purpose: Historical legally documented monetary outcomes, not a measure of toxic harm, fault, mortality or an additive company score.

USD.method: US CPI-U all items, U.S. city average, annual mean (NSA); reference 2025. 2025 BLS annual average omits October due to the federal funding lapse.

BRL.method: IBGE IPCA calendar-year Dec/Dec rates compounded after nominal base year through December 2025. The 2021 agreement was signed in February; December-2021 convention is only a standardized comparator, not a contractual indexation calculation.

CAD.method: Statistics Canada annual-average, not seasonally adjusted, Canada all-items CPI (2002=100), 2025 reference. Canada-dollar comparisons only, no exchange-rate conversion.

INR.method: India national CPI Combined (rural + urban), all items, 2012=100, 2025 calendar-year comparator. Annual indices are arithmetic means of the twelve government-published monthly index levels, rounded to three decimals. 2025 reconstructed Jan–Mar from RBI fiscal 2024-25 and Apr–Dec from RBI fiscal 2025-26. Distinct payment years must be inflation-adjusted separately; not contractual interest, legal compensation or FX conversion.

cases.hazard: 2010 oil discharge to Sneddon Creek, a Peace River tributary
cases.outcome_type: Fisheries Act environmental fine and damages-fund penalty
cases.disposition: 2015 Provincial Court guilty plea and $125,000 sentence

obligation.kind: C$113,000 to Environmental Damages Fund + C$12,000 fine; court-ordered, not independently documented as remitted

payment.detail: Environment Canada says CNRL was 'sentenced to pay' C$125,000 and uses future tense for the split between fund and fine. The public conviction registry records a sentence, not a payment receipt; completed cash disbursement is not verified in the reviewed sources.

cases.notes: Guilty plea for environmental offence and sentence are established facts; payment status is unverified. C$125,000 is a court disposition, NOT a monetized estimate of damaged fish, water or ecological services.

cases.matter: 2016 Husky North Saskatchewan River pipeline spill conviction
cases.hazard: Approximately 90,000 litres of crude oil entering North Saskatchewan River / fish and migratory birds
cases.disposition: 2019 Husky guilty plea for Fisheries Act and Migratory Birds Convention Act offences

obligation.kind: C$2.5m Fisheries Act fine + C$200,000 migratory-bird fine directed to Environmental Damages Fund

payment.detail: Canada's June 12, 2019 notice says Husky 'has been ordered to pay' C$2.7m and specifies funds 'will be directed' to the EDF; no bank or trustee receipt confirms full remittance in the reviewed source.

cases.notes: Husky Oil Operations was the legal defendant in 2019, BEFORE Husky Energy combined with Cenovus in January 2021. The Cenovus cohort association is historical-successor context only, NOT a claim that Cenovus committed the original 2016 violation or paid Husky's 2019 fine. A distinct later Husky spill case must not be combined.

sources.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada — June 2019 guilty plea and fines
Cenovus — 2021 completion of Husky combination (successor relationship only)

cases.matter: 2018 Westhazel process-water pipeline discharge Fisheries Act case
cases.hazard: Approximately 2.8 million litres of process water into the environment
cases.disposition: 2022 Husky guilty plea and sentence for Fisheries Act offence

obligation.kind: C$600,000 court-imposed fine directed to the Canadian Environmental Damages Fund

payment.detail: Canada's April 29, 2022 announcement states Husky 'was fined' C$600,000 and the fine 'will be directed' to the EDF. It is not an independently confirmed disbursement. Husky was by this point in the Cenovus group, but the named legal defendant is Husky Oil Operations Limited.

cases.notes: Not the 2016 North Saskatchewan River crude-oil pipeline case or the 2018 Newfoundland offshore White Rose case. Historic legal-entity linkage does not establish what amount, if any, Cenovus itself paid.

cases.disposition: 2024 federal Fisheries, migratory-bird and Atlantic Accord charges and court sentence

obligation.kind: C$2.4m designated to Environmental Damages Fund + C$100,000 Receiver General = total C$2.5m sentence

payment.detail: The April 26, 2024 Canadian enforcement notice says Husky was 'ordered to pay' C$2m plus C$500,000. Of the C$2.5m, C$2.4m 'will be directed' to EDF and C$100,000 to Receiver General. It does not show proof of full payment.

cases.notes: Do not add C$2m and C$2.5m as separate awards: C$2.5m already INCLUDES the C$2m component. The original spill occurred in 2018, before the 2021 Husky–Cenovus combination; index name is historical context, not an automatic finding against Cenovus.
